title: Rust: Lexer (Tokenizer)
description: Build a lexer that tokenizes source code into tokens.

steps.title: Define Token Types
steps.description: Define a `TokenType` enum with variants: `Number, Plus, Minus, Star, Slash, LParen, RParen, Ident, Keyword, Let, Print, EOF`. Define a `Token` struct with type, value, and position.
hints: `struct Token { ttype: TokenType, value: String, line: usize, col: usize }`
Tokens represent the smallest meaningful units of code.

steps.title: Lexer: Tokenize Numbers and Operators
steps.description: Create a `Lexer` struct that takes a source string. Implement `next_token() -> Token` that recognizes: digits (numbers), `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `(`, `)`, and whitespace skipping. Tokenize `"12 + 34"` and print tokens.
hints: Collect consecutive digits for Number tokens.

steps.title: Keywords and Identifiers
steps.description: Add identifier tokenization: letters followed by letters/digits. Recognize keywords like `let`, `print`. Tokenize `"let x = 42"` and print tokens.
hints: If current char is a letter, collect identifier.

steps.title: Full Tokenization Loop
steps.description: Implement `tokenize(&mut self) -> Vec<Token>` that consumes all tokens until EOF. Create a readable `display_tokens` function. Tokenize a simple program like `"let x = 10; print x * 2"` and print all tokens.

verification.failureMessage: Tokenize 'let x = 10; print x * 2' and print all tokens.

steps.title: Error Handling in Lexer
steps.description: Add error recovery: when encountering unexpected characters (like `@` or `#`), report an error and continue. Create a `LexerResult` with tokens and errors. Test with input containing invalid characters.
hints: On unexpected char, `errors.push(format!("Unexpected char '{}' at {}:{}", c, line, col))`.
Continue tokenizing after reporting the error.

verification.failureMessage: Tokenize input with errors and print both tokens and error messages.
